title: The Fuller and His Son
summary: The Third Vizier recounted a tale to teach the value of calm presence of mind:
full_text:
The Third Vizier recounted a tale to teach the value of calm presence of mind:

'Beside the swift waters of the Tigris worked an industrious fuller—a cloth-washer—and his twelve-year-old son, washing heavy woollen carpets and rolls of linen in the river.

One afternoon, while rinsing a heavy Persian carpet, the boy lost his footing upon the slippery riverbank and fell into the deep, turbulent current! The swift water swept him away, and the child cried out in terror as he was carried toward the dangerous weir.

A crowd of washermen and porters gathered upon the bank, wringing their hands, running in circles, and shouting contradictory advice, but none had the presence of mind to act.

The fuller did not waste a single breath in frantic screams. He kept his eyes locked upon his struggling son, calculated the speed of the current, seized a long, sturdy wooden drying-pole from his shop, and sprinted down the bank to a rocky spit of land fifty paces ahead of the child.

Bracing his feet firmly between two boulders, the father extended the long pole across the surface of the rushing water, shouting with calm, commanding authority: "Grasp the pole with both hands, my son, and hold fast!"

The boy reached out, locked his fingers around the sturdy wood, and the father, with steady, deliberate strength, swung the child out of the churning rapids onto the grassy bank.

The crowd cheered, praising the fuller’s bravery. The fuller embraced his shivering son and said to the spectators: "Panic is the ally of disaster; in the hour of trial, a single thought of calm reason is worth more than a thousand screams of despair."'
moral: In the face of unexpected crisis, calm presence of mind rescues what frantic panic would destroy.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Fuller and His Son"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
